title: M6 real solc-compiled OpenZeppelin ERC20 / precompile adversarial test report
lane: executor-qa-red-team (21-M4RedTeam lineage, extended to real solc-compiled bytecode)
target: evm/runtime.go Harness (real github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum v1.17.4 vm.EVM) executing REAL solc-compiled bytecode (contracts/L1Token.sol: OpenZeppelin v5 ERC20+Ownable; contracts/Precompiles.sol: a precompile-calling contract), frozen into evm/oz_erc20_fixture.go with CI-verified drift detection against a fresh compile on every run.
principle: Confirmed against real go-ethereum v1.17.4 source before any code was written: LOG0-LOG4 (core/vm/instructions.go's makeLog -> StateDB.AddLog) and all precompiles 0x1-0xa (vm.NewEVM's activePrecompiledContracts, driven by ModernChainConfig's Cancun activation) were ALREADY fully wired and working -- Harness.State is go-ethereum's own real *state.StateDB, not a custom adapter, so nothing needed to change there. The actual, sole gap was compiled bytecode: the only fixture (erc20_fixture.go) is hand-assembled because solc was never installed in this build environment; it never emits LOG opcodes at all, which is why a second, genuine gap (AddLog tagging every log with a zero-value TxHash, because Harness never called StateDB.SetTxContext) stayed unobserved until real solc output that always emits Transfer was introduced. This milestone closes both: a self-contained contracts/ Node/Hardhat project compiles real OpenZeppelin v5 contracts with pinned solc (verified locally end-to-end before any CI push -- compile+freeze from a clean rebuild reproduces byte-for-byte identical output), frozen into a checked-in Go fixture (evm/oz_erc20_fixture.go, generated programmatically from the frozen JSON to avoid hand-transcription errors in ~18KB of hex) with a freshness test (evm/oz_fixture_freshness_test.go) proving it matches; the TxHash gap is fixed in evm/runtime.go (Harness.SetTxContext wiring); and evm/oz_adversarial_test.go deploys/calls the real bytecode end to end. Unlike M1-M5's reports, production_code_modified is true here by design (the TxHash fix), same as M5's precedent for the same reason -- explained here rather than silently breaking the established convention.

adversarial_cases.scenario: Deploy contracts/L1Token.sol's real solc-compiled creation bytecode with an ABI-encoded constructor arg (initialSupply=1,000,000), call transfer(recipient, 1000) via real selector dispatch (parsed from the real ABI, not hand-encoded), read back both balances via balanceOf, then call the onlyOwner-guarded mint(recipient, 1) from a NON-owner address.
adversarial_cases.expected: Deployer starts with the full initial supply; after transfer, recipient=1000 and deployer=999999 (unchanged conservation); h.Logs() contains a real Transfer event on the token address whose Topics[0] equals the ABI's own real solc-derived event signature hash (not asserted against a hand-computed constant) with a non-zero TxHash; mint() from a non-owner reverts (real OZ Ownable require/revert path through real bytecode, not a hand-rolled shape).
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: CI run https://github.com/ITJHIT/l1chain_JIHO/actions/runs/30620890742 job 91124926194 (temporary verbose step, reverted after): '=== RUN   TestAdvEVM09OZERC20DeployMintTransferEmitsLogsWithRealTxHash' / '--- PASS: TestAdvEVM09OZERC20DeployMintTransferEmitsLogsWithRealTxHash (0.00s)'. Confirming CI run (matches the merged CI shape, non-verbose): https://github.com/ITJHIT/l1chain_JIHO/actions/runs/30620698027 job 91124307347, 'ok  l1chain/evm  0.027s'.

adversarial_cases.scenario: Sign a real message hash with a freshly generated secp256k1 key (crypto.GenerateKey + crypto.Sign), deploy contracts/Precompiles.sol's real solc-compiled bytecode, ABI-encode and call its recover(hash, v, r, s) -- which itself calls the Solidity ecrecover builtin, i.e. precompile address 0x1 -- through the real bytecode.
adversarial_cases.expected: The address returned by the real solc-compiled contract's ecrecover call, dispatched through go-ethereum's already-wired PrecompiledContractsCancun table (evm/runtime.go), matches the real signer's address exactly.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: Same CI run, verbose step: '=== RUN   TestAdvEVM10PrecompileEcrecoverViaRealSolcBytecode' / '--- PASS: TestAdvEVM10PrecompileEcrecoverViaRealSolcBytecode (0.00s)'.

adversarial_cases.scenario: Isolated, no-solc-needed synthetic proof of the SetTxContext fix on its own: minimal hand-assembled LOG0+STOP runtime bytecode, called twice.
adversarial_cases.expected: Both calls' emitted logs carry a non-zero TxHash, and the two calls' TxHash values are DIFFERENT from each other (proves a real per-call derivation, not a fixed non-zero constant that would coincidentally pass a single-call check).
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: Part of the same `l1chain/evm` package pass (see go_test_all_summary below); isolated as its own test specifically so this fix is provably exercised independent of the larger real-OZ-contract test.

adversarial_cases.scenario: Reads contracts/frozen/L1Token.json and contracts/frozen/Precompiles.json at test time (no solc needed) and asserts evm/oz_erc20_fixture.go's Go constants match exactly: ABI compared as parsed JSON (reflect.DeepEqual, not fragile raw-string equality), bytecode compared as literal strings.
adversarial_cases.expected: Exact match on both contracts, proving the checked-in Go fixture was generated correctly from the real frozen JSON.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: Part of the same `l1chain/evm` package pass; the companion CI job `Contracts (solc compile + fixture drift check)` (https://github.com/ITJHIT/l1chain_JIHO/actions/runs/30620698027 job 91124307446, pass, 20s) independently proves the frozen JSON itself is exactly what a fresh real-solc compile produces -- together these two checks close the full provenance chain from real solc output to the Go constants this milestone's tests actually execute.

summary.note: One real, small production defect found and fixed: Harness never called StateDB.SetTxContext, so every log ever emitted through this harness carried a zero-value TxHash. It was unobservable through M4 and the hand-assembled fixture (which never emits LOG opcodes at all) -- only became visible once real solc output that always emits Transfer was introduced for this milestone. Fixed in evm/runtime.go (Harness gains a monotonic txCounter; Deploy/Call each derive a distinct synthetic tx hash and call SetTxContext before executing), verified in isolation by TestHarnessTagsEmittedLogsWithARealTxHash and end-to-end by case-9's real Transfer event assertion. Everything else confirmed already correct by direct inspection of go-ethereum v1.17.4 source before any code was written: LOG opcodes and all nine precompiles (0x1-0xa) were already fully wired via the unmodified real state.StateDB and vm.NewEVM's activePrecompiledContracts -- this milestone's actual scope was narrower than the README's prior wording implied ("run solc-compiled OpenZeppelin contracts, event logs, precompiles" read as three separate gaps; only compiled bytecode and one small TxHash wiring bug were real gaps). The solc/OpenZeppelin compile pipeline itself was verified locally end-to-end (this dev sandbox has working Node/npm, unlike Go) before ever pushing to CI: npm install, hardhat compile, and the freeze script all succeeded, and a clean rebuild reproduced byte-for-byte identical frozen output, confirming the CI drift-detection job would be meaningful rather than flaky -- which it then proved on its first real CI run.

go_test_evm_verbose.note: Run as a one-off temporary CI step (this dev environment has no local Go toolchain) solely to capture real per-test evidence for this report; the step was reverted immediately after in the same PR before merge and does not appear in the merged workflow.
